statement: Submodule advancement MUST retain published contributor history, admit only descendant pins, and distinguish an unread supplier from a current supplier.
because: Leader, 2026-10-11: Goal: NO DIVERGENCE, and perfect use of github for CI/CD, handling of our code fabrication and deployment into publication.
consumer: 561-group/bare-cedar-fog and the section repositories hiring the reusable sync workflows

specification.output: one pull request retaining the existing sync branch and checked-out base history with only proven descendant pin changes
refusals: non-gitlink, deleted, ambiguous or supplier-definition base conflict
specification.baseConflictReceiving: A conflicting base merge may select only the descendant of two comparable gitlink stages, each proven to descend from their recorded common stage. Require exactly one merge base, an exact original-stage match and unchanged .gitmodules. Qualify every conflict before staging any resolution; retain both parent histories and unrelated clean merge changes. Abort and publish nothing when any condition is unresolved.
specification.publication: ordinary fast-forward push followed by authoritative ref readback; never a force push

design: Receive the existing branch and checked-out base before computing pin changes in the existing advance engine. Publish through the shared reusable workflows; gitlinks remain the parent source references. Machine deployment is a separate receiving operation.
receiving: Observe real supplier heads and ancestry against parent gitlinks; inspect the shared service PR and the parent's generated caller and mounted owner. A package check alone does not establish source or deployment convergence.
